"'''I Believe I Can Fly'''" is a song written, produced, and performed by American singer [[R. Kelly]] from the soundtrack to the 1996 film ''[[Space Jam]]''. It was originally released on November 26, 1996, and was later included on Kelly's 1998 album ''[[R. (R. Kelly album)|R.]]'' In early 1997, "I Believe I Can Fly" reached number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. It also reached the number-one spot of the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|''Billboard'' R&B Singles Chart]] and remained there for six non-consecutive weeks. Internationally, "I Believe I Can Fly" topped the charts in eight countries, including Ireland, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

The song won three awards from five nominations at the [[40th Annual Grammy Awards]]: [[Best Male R&B Vocal Performance]], [[Best R&B Song]], and [[Best Song Written for Visual Media]], while losing [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]] and [[Record of the Year]]. It was ranked number 406 on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of the [[500 Greatest Songs of All Time]] in 2004. The accompanying music video was directed by Kelly with [[Hype Williams]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=15312|title=mvdbase.com - R. Kelly - "I believe I can fly" This song hit top charts in the united states.|access-date=2014-12-02|archive-date=2016-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303212346/http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=15312|url-status=dead}}</ref> and designed by visual artist and designer [[Ron Norsworthy]].

"I Believe I Can Fly" is a song written, produced, and performed by American singer R. Kelly from the soundtrack to the 1996 film Space Jam. It was originally released on November 26, 1996, and was later included on Kelly's 1998 album R. In early 1997, "I Believe I Can Fly" reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100. It also reached the number-one spot of the Billboard R&B Singles Chart and remained there for six non-consecutive weeks. Internationally, "I Believe I Can Fly" topped the charts in eight countries, including Ireland, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

The song won three awards from five nominations at the 40th Annual Grammy Awards: Best Male R&B Vocal Performance, Best R&B Song, and Best Song Written for Visual Media, while losing Song of the Year and Record of the Year. It was ranked number 406 on Rolling Stone{{'}}s list of the 500 Greatest Songs of All Time in 2004. The accompanying music video was directed by Kelly with Hype Williams and designed by visual artist and designer Ron Norsworthy.

sections.heading: Background and composition
sections.wikitext: In a 2013 interview with The Boombox, R. Kelly was asked about the creative process behind the song: "When I met Michael Jordan on a basketball court at an athletic club — we hooped together in Chicago — he came to me and asked me if I wanted to do a song for his upcoming movie," Kelly said. "I was like, 'Yeah!' I didn't even ask what it was. [Eventually] he let me know what it was, we went to a screening to watch it and that's when I ended up coming up with 'I Believe I Can Fly'. I knew from the first melody that was gonna be the song that was gonna take me out of R&B and into another genre of music."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theboombox.com/r-kelly-i-believe-i-can-fly-interview/|title=R. Kelly Reveals Creative Process for 'I Believe I Can Fly' & Most Emotional Song Ever Written [Exclusive Interview]|last=McKynzie|first=Amber|date=December 2, 2013|website=The Boombox|access-date=August 5, 2019}}</ref> "I Believe I Can Fly" has a moderately slow [[tempo]] of 60 beats per minute, based on [[Time signature|{{Time signature|4|4}} common time]], while composed in the key of [[C major]] (with a key change to [[D-flat major|D{{music|flat}} major]]). Kelly's vocals on the track ranges from the low note of E<sub>3</sub> to the high note of A{{music|flat}}<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0153979|title=I Believe I Can Fly|first1=R.|last1=Kelly|access-date=July 17, 2025|website=www.musicnotes.com |date=August 24, 2015 }}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
A writer for ''[[Associated Press]]'' described the song as "majestic" and "[[gospel music|gospel]]-styled", noting that "hearing R. Kelly's booming voice reach a crescendo while backed up by a choir is a rousing performance that will get many replays".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_WtFAAAAIBAJ|title=R. Kelly's majestic song best on 'Space Jam' soundtrack|magazine=[[The Telegraph-Herald]]|date=December 29, 1996|access-date=March 15, 2020}}</ref> [[Larry Flick]] from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine wrote that it is "highly inspirational" and "embodying the mind-set of the two superstars [Michael Jordan and R. Kelly]". He added, "''If I can dream it, I can achieve it.'' A great motivator for the children who will flock to the silver screen for Jordan".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Larry|last=Flick|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1996/BB-1996-10-26.pdf|title=Single Reviews|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=October 26, 1996|access-date=February 5, 2020|page=80|author-link=Larry Flick}}</ref> A reviewer from ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' named it a "warm anthem".<ref>"Flying with MJ R. Kelly's anthem takes off". ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]''. November 14, 1996.</ref>

Ross Scarano from ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]'' said, "Like it or not, R. Kelly's 'I Believe I Can Fly' works because of R. Kelly. There's not another singer alive with the same combination of ability, earnest conviction, and personal demons—demons that Kelly believes he needs the listener's support to fight." He added that the singer "calls on strings and a choir and every bit of strength available in his lungs and vocal chords to rise above the broad struggle described in the lyrics."<ref>{{cite magazine|first1= Ross |last1= Scarano |title= The Best 90s R&B Songs |magazine= [[Complex (magazine)|Complex]] |date= October 8, 2019 |access-date= April 8, 2020 |url= https://www.complex.com/music/best-90s-r-b-songs/}}</ref> [[David Browne (journalist)|David Browne]] from ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' opined that the "go-for-it lyrics and florid orchestration seem to have been written with a future [[Disney]] musical in mind."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=David|last=Browne|url=https://ew.com/article/1996/11/15/music-review-space-jam/|title=Music Review: 'Space Jam'|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=November 15, 1996|access-date=February 23, 2020|author-link=David Browne (journalist)}}</ref>

Tom Ewing of [[Freaky Trigger]] noted "I Believe I Can Fly"'s "genuine power as a redemption song" and also called it "the most convincing self-help song".<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Ewing|url=http://freakytrigger.co.uk/popular/2014/02/r-kelly-i-believe-i-can-fly/#debug5|title=R. Kelly – "I Believe I Can Fly"|publisher=[[Freaky Trigger]]|date=February 23, 2014|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> British newspaper ''Lennox Herald'' named it the "undoubted highlight" of the ''Space Jam'' album".<ref>"Top Ten debut for Jam anthology". ''Lennox Herald''. July 11, 1997. page 32.</ref> Thessa Mooji from ''[[Music & Media]]'' described it as a "dramatic ballad".<ref>{{cite web|author= Mooji, Thessa |title= Reviews: Albums |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1997/MM-1997-02-01.pdf |work= [[Music & Media]] |date= February 1, 1997 |page= 15 |access-date= December 8, 2020}}</ref> ''[[Music Week]]'' rated it three out of five, calling it "a smoochy gospel-tinged ballad". The reviewer added, "A huge hit in the US and should ignite here."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=|last=|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1997/Music-Week-1997-02-22.pdf|title=Reviews: Singles|magazine=[[Music Week]]|date=February 22, 1997|page=14|accessdate=May 10, 2022}}</ref>

''[[People Magazine]]'' labeled it as "schmaltzy but potent".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://people.com/archive/picks-and-pans-review-music-from-and-inspired-by-the-space-jam-motion-picture-vol-46-no-24/|title=Picks and Pans Review: Music from and Inspired by the Space Jam Motion Picture|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|date=December 9, 1996|access-date=March 9, 2020}}</ref> ''[[Sunday Mirror]]'' gave it a full score of five out of ten, writing, "''I believe I can soar'' sings R. Kelly but I suppose we should be thankful that he's released a proper song for once instead of those awful rap cover versions which are clogging up the charts these days. It's taken from the film ''Space Jam'' and if you bought [[Toni Braxton]]'s last single and liked ''[[The Bodyguard (1992 film)|The Bodyguard]]'' then you will buy this for sure. I believe it will fly to the top of the charts though it makes me sore to say it."<ref>"The Sugar and Spice Girls Are Playing It Nice". ''[[Sunday Mirror]]''. March 2, 1997.</ref> James L. Brown from ''[[Colorado State University–Pueblo|USC Today]]'' deemed it a "long slow [[ballad]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= James L. |last= Brown |title= Space Jam rocks with new tracks |magazine= [[Colorado State University–Pueblo|USC Today]] |date= February 19, 1997 |page= 7 }}</ref>

A writer for Associated Press described the song as "majestic" and "gospel-styled", noting that "hearing R. Kelly's booming voice reach a crescendo while backed up by a choir is a rousing performance that will get many replays". Larry Flick from Billboard magazine wrote that it is "highly inspirational" and "embodying the mind-set of the two superstars [Michael Jordan and R. Kelly]". He added, "If I can dream it, I can achieve it. A great motivator for the children who will flock to the silver screen for Jordan". A reviewer from Chicago Sun-Times named it a "warm anthem".

Ross Scarano from Complex said, "Like it or not, R. Kelly's 'I Believe I Can Fly' works because of R. Kelly. There's not another singer alive with the same combination of ability, earnest conviction, and personal demons—demons that Kelly believes he needs the listener's support to fight." He added that the singer "calls on strings and a choir and every bit of strength available in his lungs and vocal chords to rise above the broad struggle described in the lyrics." David Browne from Entertainment Weekly opined that the "go-for-it lyrics and florid orchestration seem to have been written with a future Disney musical in mind."

Tom Ewing of Freaky Trigger noted "I Believe I Can Fly"'s "genuine power as a redemption song" and also called it "the most convincing self-help song". British newspaper Lennox Herald named it the "undoubted highlight" of the Space Jam album". Thessa Mooji from Music & Media described it as a "dramatic ballad". Music Week rated it three out of five, calling it "a smoochy gospel-tinged ballad". The reviewer added, "A huge hit in the US and should ignite here."

People Magazine labeled it as "schmaltzy but potent". Sunday Mirror gave it a full score of five out of ten, writing, "I believe I can soar sings R. Kelly but I suppose we should be thankful that he's released a proper song for once instead of those awful rap cover versions which are clogging up the charts these days. It's taken from the film Space Jam and if you bought Toni Braxton's last single and liked The Bodyguard then you will buy this for sure. I believe it will fly to the top of the charts though it makes me sore to say it." James L. Brown from USC Today deemed it a "long slow ballad".

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video for "I Believe I Can Fly" was directed by [[Hype Williams]]. It begins at an old farm, where a young boy is playing with his ball. By the farm lies an autumn yellow cornfield, where R. Kelly starts singing. In another scene, a large screen by the farm is showing clips from ''[[Space Jam]]'', while Kelly performs on the ground. Later in the video, the singer sits in an autumn forest. Behind him is the screen where the film's clips are displayed. In the last part of the video, Kelly conducts a large choir in a sports hall, accompanied by an orchestra. After Kelly has sung the last stanzas of the song, the choir claps as the video ends.<ref name=musicvideo>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIQn8pab8Vc |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131031050834/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIQn8pab8Vc&list=UUZZjtPu39XM1ujnfzooh-ew |archive-date=2013-10-31 |url-status=dead|title=R. Kelly - I Believe I Can Fly (LP Version)|work=[[YouTube]]|access-date=1 August 2020}} ({{web archive |url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/GIQn8pab8Vc |date=21 September 2021 }})</ref>

The official music video was published to YouTube in October 2013, where it remained until the termination of his channel in October 2021.<ref name=musicvideo /><ref>{{cite web |title=R. Kelly's YouTube channels removed after conviction |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-58815087 |access-date=28 June 2025 |date=6 October 2021}}</ref>

sections.heading: In film and television
sections.wikitext:
Other than appearing on the soundtrack for the film ''[[Space Jam]]'', "I Believe I Can Fly" was performed by the school band in the 2002 film ''[[Drumline (film)|Drumline]]'' during the high school graduation ceremony of Devon Miles (played by [[Nick Cannon]]). 
*In the 2006 ''[[Ice Age (2002 film)|Ice Age]]'' animated sequel film ''[[Ice Age 2: The Meltdown]]'', by [[20th Century Fox Animation|20th Century Fox]] and [[Blue Sky Studios]], [[List of Ice Age characters#Crash|Crash]] the [[opossum|possum]] (voiced by [[Seann William Scott]]) briefly sings the song after [[Manny (Ice Age)|Manny]] the [[woolly mammoth]] (voiced by [[Ray Romano]]) catapults him with a tree before he crashes into another. 
*In the 2003 film ''[[Good Boy!]]'', Wilson briefly sings the song while diving into a pool. 
*In the first-season episode of the television series ''[[Da Ali G Show]]'', [[Ali G]] performs the song during the opening skit.
*In the 2005 comedy ''[[Fun with Dick and Jane (2005 film)|Fun with Dick and Jane]]'', Jim Carrey sings along with the song as it is played in an elevator. 
*This song also appeared on the [[The X Factor (U.S. season 1)|first American season]] of ''[[The X Factor (U.S.)|The X Factor]]'', where R. Kelly performed "I Believe I Can Fly" for the first time as a duet with the eventual winner of the show is [[Melanie Amaro]]. 
*This song was also performed on the singing competition series ''[[The Voice (U.S.)|The Voice]]'' as the last solo song for the [[The Voice (U.S. season 2)|Season 2]] winner [[Jermaine Paul]].
*In the Fox musical television series ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', performed a version of the song in episode fourteen of [[Glee season 3|season three]], "[[On My Way (Glee)|On My Way]]" (aired on February 21, 2012). It is a mash-up track with the song "[[Fly (Nicki Minaj song)|Fly]]" by [[Nicki Minaj]] featuring [[Rihanna]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://perezhilton.com/tv/GLEE_The_New_Directions_Perform_Fly_I_Believe_I_Can_Fly/?id=54a9fb8ce6011&autoplay=false|title=GLEE: The New Directions Perform Fly/I Believe I Can Fly on Perez TV|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203223617/http://perezhilton.com/tv/GLEE_The_New_Directions_Perform_Fly_I_Believe_I_Can_Fly/?id=54a9fb8ce6011&autoplay=false|archive-date=2013-12-03}}</ref>
*In the comedy's third installment ''[[The Hangover Part III]]'', Leslie Chow sings a 12-second portion of the song, while parachuting through [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]].
*In [[Red Velvet (band)|Red Velvet's]] ''Level Up Project'', [[Wendy Shon]] sang the chorus while [[parasailing]] and riding on a speed boat in [[Pattaya]], [[Thailand]]. She also sang the chorus in Level Up Project 2 in 2017-2018 and in ''[[Battle Trip]]''{{'}}s Episode 103 while [[paragliding]] in [[Krems an der Donau]], Austria.

sections.heading: Other performances
sections.wikitext:
Kelly performed this song at the [[40th Annual Grammy Awards]].

In The TP-2.com Tour, Kelly performed a 10-minute long remix of "I Believe I Can Fly," which included dialogue from a priest, Kelly's mother, and God as characters. The remix was later featured on the [[Bootleg recording|bootleg]] release ''[[R. Kelly#2002–2003: The Best of Both Worlds and Chocolate Factory|Loveland]]''.<ref name="The New York Times">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/09/08/arts/the-new-season-music-the-adventures-of-loveland.html|title=THE NEW SEASON/MUSIC; The Adventures Of 'Loveland'|last=Sanneh|first=Kelefa|website=The New York Times|date=8 Sep 2002|access-date=25 Jul 2018}}</ref><ref name="MTV">{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1454446/r-kelly-vows-to-clamp-down-as-new-bootleg-hits-streets/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814105741/http://www.mtv.com/news/1454446/r-kelly-vows-to-clamp-down-as-new-bootleg-hits-streets/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2014|title=R. Kelly Vows To Clamp Down As New Bootleg Hits Streets|website=MTV|date=21 May 2002|access-date=25 Jul 2018}}</ref>

[[STS-122]] crew heard this song on flight day 10 as a wake up call.<ref name="wakeup">{{cite web|url=http://spaceflight1.nasa.gov/gallery/audio/shuttle/sts-122/html/ndxpage1.html|title=STS-122 Wakeup Calls|access-date=February 16, 2008|publisher=NASA|year=2008|author=NASA|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080217205720/http://spaceflight1.nasa.gov/gallery/audio/shuttle/sts-122/html/ndxpage1.html|archive-date=February 17, 2008}}</ref>

Since its release, it has become commonly associated with the [[NBA]], most notably with [[Michael Jordan]]. The song also played at the conclusion of [[NBA on NBC|NBC]]'s broadcast of the [[1997 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{YouTube|wPg6WcXk6JM|1997 NBA Finals Tribute}}</ref>

In addition to the NBA, the song also found use at other sporting events, most notably at [[Major League Baseball]]'s [[New York Yankees]] home games during their four consecutive World Series runs from [[1998 World Series|1998]] to [[2001 World Series|2001]], the first three of which they won. Also was used in the NFL for the Atlanta Falcons during their pregame in the late 1990s - early 2000s.

A version of the song, recorded by the Halifax community choir, was used as the backing track to a 2012 UK TV advertisement for the [[Halifax Bank]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thedrum.co.uk/news/2012/02/21/halifax-unveil-home-insurance-ad-adam-and-eve |title=Halifax unveil home insurance ad with Adam and Eve |publisher=The Drum |access-date=2012-11-08}}</ref>

On October 13, 2012, when the [[Space Shuttle Endeavour]] was being transferred from [[Los Angeles International Airport]] to the [[California Science Center]] through the streets of [[Los Angeles]], the recording was played as the shuttle left [[The Forum (Inglewood)|The Forum]], and the song was performed live by [[James Ingram]] later that day at [[Debbie Allen]]'s live show celebrating the Endeavour's arrival at the corner of [[Crenshaw, Los Angeles|Crenshaw Blvd and Martin Luther King Blvd]]. (The shuttle was delayed over five hours in arriving there; to keep the crowd entertained, the performance went on only slightly delayed.)

*In the 1999 episode "The Best of Both Worlds" of the Nickelodeon animated television series ''[[KaBlam!]]'', in the ''[[Life with Loopy]]'' segment, the song was spoofed - in name only - as "I (Don't) Believe I Can Fly."<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6NRuesptp4M ''KABLAM!'' Smith |last2=Adams |first2=Yolanda |author2-link=Yolanda Adams |title=Yolanda Adams: "I Believe I Can Fly" (32nd Dove Awards) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N284bg3_q0k |website=youtube.com |publisher=[[GMA Dove Awards]] |language=en |format=video |date=May 25, 2021|access-date=February 15, 2026}}</ref> and in 2002 with the  Soul Children of Chicago at The Concert for World Children's Day [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] TV special.<ref>{{cite web|title=What Do We Do Now with ‘I Believe I Can Fly?’: EUR Video Throwback|url=https://eurweb.com/what-do-we-do-now-with-i-believe-i-can-fly-eur-video-throwback/|work=eurweb.com|access-date=February 25, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Concert for World Children's Day (TV Special 2002) - IMDb|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0381103/|work=[[IMDb]]|access-date=February 15, 2026}}</ref> In 2026, Adams' version was certified Gold in New Zealand, making it [[List of best-selling gospel music artists#New Zealand|one of the best-selling gospel songs in the region]].<ref name="YolandaNZ"/>

The album contains a studio version featuring Gerald Levert and a live solo recording which were both issued as singles. In 2001, she performed the song with the Nashville Super Choir at the 32nd GMA Dove Awards and in 2002 with the  Soul Children of Chicago at The Concert for World Children's Day ABC TV special. In 2026, Adams' version was certified Gold in New Zealand, making it one of the best-selling gospel songs in the region. 

In 2005, a cover by Kenny G featuring Adams was released as a single in 2005, from his US Gold-certified album At Last...The Duets Album (2004).
